newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks expected soft on Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks expected soft on Wall Street fall.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to open easier on Monday following a sharp fall on Wall Street on Friday, hit by renewed fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates, brokers said.

"The market should see some pressure since the Dow dropped nearly 140 points," said Edwin Cheung, dealing director at Taiwan Securities. "But a substantial correction is unlikely and the index should find good support at the 13,800 mark."
Brokers said trading would likely be range-bound ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, which sets U.S. interest rate levels.
The Hang Seng Index rose 20.47 points to 14,062.37 on Friday. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index eased 5.05 points to 14,057.32.
Andrew To, dealing director of OSK Asia Securities, said trade might slow, with individual blue chips and red chips seen attracting buyers.
"HSBC Holdings is likely to continue to rise on arbitrage buying due to firmer sterling," he said.
